findings.title: Windows can leave Argon2 blocks outside error-report exclusion
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Requires Windows, registration exhaustion or a high memory level, and a crash/report during Argon2; no direct secret compromise was demonstrated
findings.reproduction: The 32-bit registration size and 512-entry process limit require 513 blocks at level 20 and 769 at level 21. Registration stops at the first refusal while engine construction still succeeds. Separately, 512 simultaneously live Secret values consume the quota before a small work area is created. aud005 source-findings checks the exact arithmetic and source contracts.
findings.expected: The whole work area is excluded as SECURITY.md promises, or construction refuses/exposes a required security decision before secret input.
findings.observed: Level 20 leaves 512 bytes uncovered; level 21 leaves 1,099,511,628,288 bytes uncovered. After 512 other live registrations, a 65,536-byte work area has no covered block. NativeArgon2 exposes is_locked but not the failed dump coverage.
findings.impact: A Windows error report during Argon2 can include unregistered secret-derived blocks and make password candidates cheaper to test. No original phrase/password disclosure, actual dump or cross-platform impact was demonstrated.
evidence: Source locations and Microsoft WerRegisterExcludedMemoryBlock contract
findings.recommendedFix: Require complete WER exclusion before worker startup or secret input, or expose an explicit mandatory status and narrow the documented guarantee. Account for every live registration.
findings.requiredVerification: On Windows, cover 512 live Secret values, the 513/769 arithmetic, refusal/status before Argon2, drop/unregister balance and thread-construction failure without a secret-dependent fallback.

findings.title: Cancellation guidance can release an unchecked container and repair card
findings.releaseBlockingReason: The guidance violates the mandatory creation-check contract, but no incorrect transformation or corrupt container was demonstrated
affectedBuilds: All hosts following the API guidance
findings.reproduction: Continue from on_unchecked and Break at round 13. Production Mhfe::encrypt returns Ok(ControlFlow::Break(())) before the reverse comparison, while repair rustdoc and SECURITY.md permit release once encrypt returns Ok. The audit executes this exact callback sequence with a public synthetic engine.
findings.expected: NEW-5/NEW-6 keep a cancelled container unverified and forbid program release before the check passes. RPR-1 releases a repair card only after the creation check passes. Publication requires Ok(ControlFlow::Continue(_)).
findings.observed: Ok(Break) satisfies the documented release condition without verification. The error-module header also still names cancellation after Error::Cancelled was removed.
findings.impact: A host can publish an unchecked container and repair card as finished backups instead of reporting cancellation. No wrong Feistel result or direct secret compromise was demonstrated.
findings.recommendedFix: Require Ok(ControlFlow::Continue(_)) in both publication conditions, describe Break as unverified and remove cancellation from the error-module summary. Coordinate host documentation.
findings.requiredVerification: Add production-path cancellation regressions/doctests at on_unchecked and the first reverse-check round; require no final publication on Break, publication only on Continue and correct engine reuse. Check mhfe and browser consumers.

findings.title: NFKD byte counting overflows before password-length refusal on 32-bit targets
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Large-input denial of service without memory corruption, truncated-password acceptance or secret compromise
affectedBuilds: Shared passphrase/draw callers of the same helper
findings.reproduction: Repeat U+FDFA 130,150,525 times: 390,451,575 input bytes expand to 4,294,967,325 bytes (2^32 + 29). The usize count wraps to 29 on a 32-bit target and enters the success path before a bounds panic; checked builds can panic during counting. The preceding repetition count fits u32 and reaches PasswordTooLong.
findings.expected: PW-5 and Password::new refuse every normalized password over 1,024 bytes before writing, never truncate it and do not panic on outside input.
findings.observed: Source arithmetic proves the 32-bit overflow and undersized write attempt. The audit did not execute a 32-bit runtime; runtimeExecuted is false in finding-probes.json.
findings.impact: Input-triggered denial of service. Rust bounds checks prevent memory corruption and no truncated password or seed is returned. The roughly 372 MiB input requirement limits practical severity.
findings.recommendedFix: Use checked or saturating accumulation and return the over-limit outcome as soon as the relevant limit is exceeded, preserving admitted NFKD bytes and the separate BIP39 passphrase contract.
findings.requiredVerification: Run exact boundary and preceding control on 32-bit WebAssembly in release and checked builds; require non-panicking refusal before allocation/writing and recheck 0, 1, 1,024 and 1,025 normalized bytes.

findings.title: README omits the WebAssembly exception to its 64-bit requirement
findings.reproduction: Compare the unconditional 64-bit requirement in README.md with the following browser sentence, explicit 32-bit WebAssembly rustdoc and CI WASM target.
findings.expected: Distinguish the native engine's 64-bit restriction from supported 32-bit WebAssembly with a host engine.
findings.observed: The README can lead a WebAssembly integrator to reject a supported target.
findings.impact: Limited documentation defect; no runtime or protocol effect.
evidence: Fast WASM Clippy and CI WASM job definition
findings.recommendedFix: State that native builds need 64-bit, while 32-bit WebAssembly is supported with a host Argon2id engine and suitable memory limits.
findings.requiredVerification: Compare revised wording with native compile_error!, WASM rustdoc and CI target coverage while retaining the memory qualification.

findings.title: Stack scanner can treat unread pages as a clean result
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Verification-tool false success, not a demonstrated production stack residue
findings.reproduction: Two scan paths discard read_exact_at results into zero-initialized buffers. The read helper anticipates guard-page failures. The wrapper checks only a completion marker and zero stack-hit lines and never requires known control hits.
findings.expected: Unexpected read failure and absent positive controls prevent a passing verification verdict under CORE-22/CORE-28 and the remaining AUD-004-BLD001 acceptance requirement.
findings.observed: source-findings confirms two ignored read-result sites and no wrapper positive-control requirement. Unexpected unread pages can therefore produce the same zero-hit verdict as a clean completed scan.
findings.impact: A maintainer can accept an erasure check that did not read secret-bearing pages. No current production residue is established; independent fast memory tests passed.
evidence: Source control flow; no fault injection or new stack scan executed
findings.recommendedFix: Track read coverage, fail on unexpected errors, classify permitted guard pages separately and require expected positive-control hits before accepting zero production hits.
findings.requiredVerification: Require nonzero for unexpected read errors, incomplete coverage, absent controls, crash, timeout and malformed output; require zero only for a complete controlled clean scan.

remediation.evidence: Fixed in the commit that adds this record. SECURITY.md states the limit of the 512 Windows exclusions, and NativeArgon2::is_out_of_dumps says whether all of the work area is excluded. In practice only a host holding about 500 Secrets reaches it: memory levels 20 and 21 need 2 and 3 TiB, which Windows does not commit on real machines.

Fixed in the commit that adds this record. SECURITY.md, src/repair.rs and Mhfe::encrypt name Ok(ControlFlow::Continue(_)) as the condition for giving out a container and its card; a test stops in the first round of the check and gets Break with the container shown unchecked; src/error.rs no longer names cancellation.

Fixed in the commit that adds this record. Nfkd::of counts with saturating addition, so a text whose NFKD passes the address space of a 32-bit target is refused as PasswordTooLong before anything is written.
Fixed in the commit that adds this record. The README says that a native build needs a 64-bit target and that in 32-bit WebAssembly the program supplies Argon2id.

Fixed in the commit that adds this record. probe-stack ends on a stack page it cannot read and counts the unreadable pages of the writable mappings; run-matrix.sh requires the probe's own copies of the secrets to be found. The default scan passes with 38 hits on 40 calls and no stack hits. This completes AUD-004-BLD001, whose positive control was missing.
